The disqualification bit is the negated pointed-to opponent bit.

inspection.type:
∀ {k t : ℕ} {C : QuarticQuery.Circuit (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord k t)} (n : ℕ)
  (x : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.Upper.Loc k t C)) (i j : QuarticQuery.Upper.Col t) (hij : i < j),
  QuarticQuery.Upper.cmpProb n x i j =
    ∑ s₁,
      QuarticQuery.Upper.addrLaw n x i s₁ *
        ∑ s₂,
          QuarticQuery.Upper.addrLaw n x j s₂ *
            if
                QuarticQuery.Upper.firstWins (QuarticQuery.Upper.disq x i s₁ j ⋯) (QuarticQuery.Upper.disq x j s₂ i ⋯) =
                  Bool.true then
              1
            else 0

lean.note: Gives exact smaller-index outcome law as a sum over decoded addresses and the disqualification rule. The self case, physical circuit, and exact definition of the tie-breaking rule are separate.

premises: Arbitrary repetition count and selected column.

inspection.type:
∀ {k t : ℕ} {C : QuarticQuery.Circuit (QuarticQuery.ForrelationCoord k t)},
  1 ≤ k →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) (i j : QuarticQuery.Upper.Col t),
      ∃ Z x o out F,
        QuarticQuery.Upper.IsCirc (QuarticQuery.Upper.cmpCost k t n) F ∧
          (QuarticQuery.Upper.IsCirc (QuarticQuery.Upper.cmpCost k t n) fun x_1 => (F x_1).symm) ∧
            ∀ (x_1 : QuarticQuery.BitInput (QuarticQuery.Upper.Loc k t C)) (b : Bool),
              QuarticQuery.Upper.lawOf ((F x_1) (QuarticQuery.Upper.rket o)) out b =
                QuarticQuery.Upper.bern (QuarticQuery.Upper.cmpProb n x_1 i j) b

presentation.body: For two distinct columns, first sort them and decode each in a separate workspace. At each decoded address, read the column’s pointer toward its opponent and inspect the selected bit of the opponent’s data string. A column disqualifies its opponent when that bit is zero. If exactly one column disqualifies the other, that column wins; otherwise, the smaller index wins. A self-comparison returns false without reading a pointer.

statement: Comparison of distinct columns, in sorted order: decode each in separate workspaces; read each column's pointer towards the other at its decoded address and inspect the pointed bit of the other's X string. A column disqualifies its opponent if that bit is 0. If exactly one disqualifies the other it is victorious, otherwise the smaller index. A self-comparison returns false without reading a pointer.
